comments.body:
Follow-up work scoped out for this PR:

I think `systemd.services.print-host-key` should be factored out into a separate module. It's not EC2-specific, but useful on any platform with an externally machine-readable serial log.
If anything, it's `ssh/sshd.nix`-adjacent, so around there would be a natural location.

(And in a modular service, it would even be part of the `sshd` service module as a sub-service, but that's not relevant for now)

Would this make the functionality in https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/444040#issuecomment-3308153529 obsolete?   Our AMI has some obscure feature to pre-provision the host-key through user-data which I really want to remove (As it's a terrible idea security wise).

The way this works is that the key gets generated on the instance, so the private key isn't handled by anything else.
So no pre-provisioning; just a secure host public key retrieval method.

I imagine the main benefit vs what you're suggesting is that this method requires no other infrastructure to be set up, making it more robust and perhaps easier to configure.

An SSH CA seems mostly independent of key generation, so I imagine you could do both:
1. host key in deployment tool's state for setup
2. CA for other clients' benefit.

> Our AMI has some obscure feature to pre-provision the host-key through user-data which I really want to remove (As it's a terrible idea security wise).

I kind of don't want to argue for making things less secure, but technically pre-provisioning through user data can be faster, because you can configure the client concurrently with server setup. That's not an overriding reason except in pretty limited circumstances, like perhaps automated testing in an account and VPC that are isolated and everything is torn down when done.

> TODO
> 
> * [ ]  Validation with nixops4

Probably won't get around to this for another while, so if you want to have this earlier, feel free to merge.

review_comments.body:
You're confusing concepts here.   IMDSv1 has to do with the authentication mechanism; not with the `1.0` uri.    IMDSv2 also has the 1.0 endpoints.  it just doesn't allow you to access the URI without a token.

We dont' support IMDSv1 in the NixOS images at all anymore

@@ -0,0 +1,266 @@
+# Run with:
+#   cd nixpkgs
+#   nix-build -A nixosTests.ec2-image
+
+{
+  config,
+  lib,
+  hostPkgs,
+  ...
+}:
+
+let
+  inherit (lib) mkAfter mkForce;
+  pkgs = config.node.pkgs;
+
+  # Build an EC2 image configuration
+  imageCfg =
+    (import ../lib/eval-config.nix {
+      system = null;
+      modules = [
+        ../maintainers/scripts/ec2/amazon-image.nix
+        ../modules/testing/test-instrumentation.nix
+        ../modules/profiles/qemu-guest.nix
+        {
+          amazonImage.format = "qcow2";
+
+          # In a NixOS test the serial console is occupied by the "backdoor"
+          # (see testing/test-instrumentation.nix) and is incompatible with
+          # the configuration in virtualisation/amazon-image.nix.
+          systemd.services."serial-getty@ttyS0".enable = mkForce false;
+
+          # Make /dev/console point to serial console for proper capture
+          # test-instrumentation.nix adds console=tty0, so we need to add console=ttyS0 AFTER it
+          # The last console= parameter takes precedence for /dev/console
+          boot.kernelParams = mkAfter [ "console=ttyS0" ];
+
+          # Configure VLAN networking to match test framework setup
+          networking.interfaces.eth0 = {
+            ipv4.addresses = [
+              {
+                address = config.nodes.machine.networking.primaryIPAddress;
+                prefixLength = 24;
+              }
+            ];
+          };
+
+          nixpkgs.pkgs = pkgs;
+        }
+      ];
+    }).config;
+
+  image = "${imageCfg.system.build.amazonImage}/${imageCfg.image.fileName}";
+
+in
+{
+  name = "ec2-image";
+  meta = {
+    maintainers = with lib.maintainers; [
+      roberth
+      arianvp
+    ];
+    timeout = 600;
+  };
+  skipTypeCheck = true; # Disable type checking due to MAC address parsing issues
+  skipLint = true; # Disable linting due to MAC address parsing issues
+
+  nodes = {
+    machine = { ... }: { }; # Dummy node for network config - won't be launched
+    client =
+      { ... }:
+      {
+        # Configure SSH client for non-interactive, strict authentication
+        programs.ssh.extraConfig = ''
+          Host *
+            PasswordAuthentication no
+            ChallengeResponseAuthentication no
+            HostbasedAuthentication no
+            BatchMode yes
+            PubkeyAuthentication yes
+            StrictHostKeyChecking yes
+        '';
+      };
+  };
+
+  testScript = ''
+    import os
+    import re
+    import subprocess
+    import tempfile
+
+    # Instance Metadata Service
+    # FIXME: Support IMDSv2
+    #        - Consider https://github.com/aws/amazon-ec2-metadata-mock, or
+    #        - Consider https://github.com/purpleclay/imds-mock
+    #        - Use IMDSv2 to provide the client's pubkey to the instance
+    #        - [Test matrix] also test providing the host key through IMDS
+    #          - i.e. a test module argument to select between writing or reading the host key
+    def create_ec2_metadata_dir(temp_dir, client_pubkey):
+        """Create fake EC2 metadata directory structure with mock data"""
+        metadata_dir = os.path.join(temp_dir.name, "ec2-metadata")
+
+        # Create directory structure
+        os.makedirs(os.path.join(metadata_dir, "1.0", "meta-data", "public-keys", "0"), exist_ok=True)
+        os.makedirs(os.path.join(metadata_dir, "latest", "api"), exist_ok=True)
+
+        # IMDS v1 endpoints (what fetch-ec2-metadata.sh actually fetches)

review_comments.body: What you are implementing here is indeed IMDSv2. But with the  `1.0` version of the metadata
